messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The markets are running as usual, but something’s off—people are moving quietly, the usual noise is gone, and even the phone’s been acting up. Best to keep plans light and stay close to home for now."
Sender 2: "Just heard the pharmacy on 3rd Street ran out of insulin again — strange, since they just got a new shipment last week. Thought you should know."
Sender 3: "The markets are full, the trains run on time, but something feels off — people are talking in the open, and the silence from the top is louder than any announcement. Be careful who you meet, and keep your eyes on the quiet ones."
Sender 4: "The weather’s been strange this season—late rains, early chill—but people are starting to notice the patterns. Best to keep things quiet, stay close to home, and be ready to move if needed."
Sender 5: "Hey — just wanted to say I’ve been keeping an eye on things, and the quiet stuff is piling up. The usual signs aren’t just whispers anymore; even the ones who used to stay silent are talking about next year’s plans. We should stay sharp, but keep it low. Nothing to act on yet — just… prepare quietly."
Sender 6: "The air’s different lately—people are talking, even strangers. Seems like everyone’s waiting for something, just not sure what. Keep your head down, but don’t look away."
Sender 7: "Just heard a quiet word from someone we trust — the usual channels aren’t just whispering, they’re speaking openly now. Best to keep things low, but the air’s changed. We’ll talk when we can."
Sender 8: "The city’s been quiet lately—like it’s holding its breath. I’ve been hearing the same thing from a few trusted people: things are shifting, and no one’s pretending otherwise anymore."
Sender 9: "Just got back from the market—there’s a strange quiet in the air, like everyone’s holding their breath. I heard the schoolteachers are still waiting on pay, but no one’s talking about it like they used to. Strangest thing: my neighbor asked me last week, “What would you do if things changed?” — never once brought up politics before. Things feel… loose."
Sender 10: "Just got back from the market — everything’s normal, kids laughing, bread fresh. Feels like the quiet before something happens, but we’re all pretending it’s just another week. Be careful what you say, even here."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
